result.summary: Adds several systemd sandboxing and hardening directives to the bitcoind systemd service file in contrib/init. These settings configure kernel, clock, and hostname protections, namespace, realtime, and SUID restrictions, a socket address family allowlist, an empty capability bounding set, and system call filtering. It also changes the ExecStartPre chgrp prefix modifier from exclamation mark to plus so the pre-exec command retains required privileges under the new capability limits.
result.problem: Linux systems running bitcoind via the provided systemd service unit lack defense-in-depth sandboxing, leaving the daemon process with unnecessary kernel, capability, and namespace privileges if compromised.
evidence: Author notes the service currently lacks sandboxing options that bitcoind does not need to be exempt from, such as kernel/clock/hostname protection and SUID restrictions (PR description)
Author identifies that without switching the ExecStartPre prefix to '+', the new syscall filter and capability bounding set would block the startup chgrp invocation (PR description)
result.scope_notes: Touches only the contrib/init systemd service configuration file. Reviewers should verify compatibility with older systemd versions supported by downstream distributions.
result.card: Adds systemd hardening and sandboxing directives to the example bitcoind systemd service unit in contrib/init, restricting system calls, namespaces, capabilities, and socket families. Deployments using the provided systemd service currently run without process-level sandboxing, allowing an attacker who compromises the daemon access to unnecessary system interfaces. The author notes that bitcoind does not require these privileges to operate normally and updates the ExecStartPre prefix so initial directory ownership setup continues to function under the restricted capability set. No dependencies are recorded.
uncertainties: The patch diff was omitted, though the description explicitly enumerates the directives added to the unit file.

risk.why: Incorrect or incompatible systemd directives could cause bitcoind to fail to start on distributions running older systemd releases.
